general_information.Description: The course gives students a working understanding of how modern generative AI models work and how to use them well. The course covers foundations and intuition of large language models, diffusion and multimodal models; prompt engineering and evaluation; retrieval-augmented generation (RAG); building applications with model APIs; agents and tool use; customization (prompting, RAG, fine-tuning); failure modes and evaluation; and ethics, safety, and governance. Mathematical internals are deferred to the Deep Learning course; this course stays at the level of intuition while building real, hands-on skill.
general_information.StudentTasks: - Students must attend at least 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination. - Students are responsible for completing all exercises, labs, and the term project given by the instructor, in class or at home, and submitting on time. - Use laptop in class only for learning purposes. - Promptly access the FU FLM at https://flm.fpt.edu.vn/ for up-to-date course information. - Disclose any use of AI tools as required by each assignment, and be able to explain and defend all submitted work.
general_information.Tools: - Any modern chat-based AI assistant (free tier acceptable for most labs) - Python 3.10+ with Google Colab or Jupyter Notebook - A code/text editor (e.g., VS Code) - A model API endpoint provided by the instructor for Lab 3 (mock available offline)
general_information.Note: 1) On-going Assessment - 2 Labs: 10% (Labs 1-2, each 5%) - Progress Test: 10% - Project Proposal: 10% - Final Project: 30% 2) 1 Final Exam: 40% 3) Final Result: 100% Completion Criteria: 1) Every on-going assessment component > 0 2) Term Project > 0 3) Final Exam Score >= 4 & Final Result >= 5

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Describe how generative AI models work at an intuitive, non-mathematical level.
Apply prompt engineering techniques to obtain useful, reliable outputs from generative models.

Build a small generative AI application end to end, retrieval-augmented generation, structured output validation, basic agent/tool use, and an appropriate customization strategy (prompting, RAG, or fine-tuning).
Evaluate generative AI outputs and systems using rubrics, test sets, model-as-judge methods, and analysis of failure modes.
Analyze the ethical, social, legal, and governance implications of generative AI and apply responsible-use practices.
